Sizes are bytes in one proof of the same 32,768-signature batch; they do not depend on the thread count. kB and MB are decimal (1 kB = 1,000 bytes). The parts are what each harness reports: BitZ's proof payload breakdown, and Aerie's envelope split into salts, commitments, the Akita opening and everything else (header and PIOP messages).

Aerie's default proof carries every signature's 40-byte salt, 1.31 MB at this batch, because its verifier recomputes HashToPoint from it. When all signers share one salt the PIOP and opening are unchanged, so the proof is 68.0 kB (66.4 KiB). That row is derived from the measured per-record proof by removing the per-record salts.
BitZ's statement takes the HashToPoint targets as public inputs, so its proof carries no salts; a verifier still needs the salts or the targets from somewhere.

BitZ's bridge sends one integer column sum per bridge column, in the clear. With John's 2^13 bridge rows, 32,768 signatures give 65,536 columns of 20-byte sums: 1.31 MB, three quarters of the proof. The experiment uses one limb and 2^16 rows, so the same batch has 8,192 columns of 16-byte sums, 131 kB. Each extra row variable halves the column count; in exchange, one limb at 2^16 rows needs a smaller sampled prime (2^111 ≤ p < 2^112), which costs more proof-of-work per prime-field round.

The experiment's keyed ring check sends 4.2 kB of exact quotient values, where the canonical check sent 96 bytes of carries. BitZ also sends a 2-byte exception count per signature (65.5 kB), although no coefficient in this batch needed an exception; a sparse list would remove almost all of it.

The opening is now BitZ's largest part. In both versions, Merkle authentication paths take about 218 kB (58% of the opening) and opened rows 144 kB (38%), split between the first commitment and the recursive Ligerito levels. The opening uses the unique-decoding query count, so fewer queries would shrink both. The opening's split comes from a bench-only breakdown of the serialized Ligerito proof; its parts sum exactly to the reported size.
